stem_book: In Column-I certain situations are depicted. In all cases there is a uniform solid cylinder on a rough plank, the plank resting on a smooth floor. Assume friction is sufficient for pure rolling. The mass of the cylinder is equal to that of the plank. Match with appropriate descriptions in Column-II. Column-I: (A) horizontal force F (to the right) applied at the top of the cylinder; (B) a clockwise couple applied on the cylinder; (C) horizontal force F (to the right) applied at the centre of the cylinder; (D) horizontal force F (to the right) applied on the plank. Column-II: (P) Plank accelerates to the left (Q) Friction on cylinder is towards right (R) Friction on cylinder is in direction opposite to its acceleration (S) The acceleration of cylinder is greater in magnitude than that of the plank (T) Acceleration of cylinder is towards right. (a) (A)-PQST, (B)-PQT, (C)-RST, (D)-QT (b) (A)-PQT, (B)-PQRT, (C)-RST, (D)-QT (c) (A)-PQST, (B)-PQT, (C)-QT, (D)-RST (d) (A)-PQRST, (B)-PRS, (C)-RST, (D)-QT
reason: situations exist only as drawings (plus 'smooth' floor); described in words, solid cylinder assumed
work: A: f = F/4 →, a_c = 5F/4m →, a_p = F/4m ← (PQST); B: f = C/2R →, a_c = a_p = C/2mR opposite (PQT); C: f = F/4 ←, a_c = 3F/4m, a_p = F/4m → (RST); D: f = F/4 →, a_c = F/4m, a_p = 3F/4m (QT)
